channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
item.description: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
item.description: Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
item.description: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine and the US: What's next after Trump's diesel deal with Russia?
item.description: Donald Trump plans to allow the purchase of Russian diesel, drawing criticism at home and abroad. What is behind the US president's decision and what should Ukraine do next? DW spoke with experts.

item.title: [DW] Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
item.description: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move but critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.

item.title: [DW] Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
item.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

item.title: [DW] What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
item.description: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

item.title: [EU Observer] Pressure mounts on EU leaders to strike a budget deal by December
item.description: EU Council president Antonio Costa has been tasked to deliver a new compromise before EU leaders meet again on 26 November in Brussels, with the aim to strike a deal during the summit in December - after the Irish proposal failed to gain any support.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU is bankrolling border drones while starving the watchdogs meant to stop abuses
item.description: Millions of euros of EU funds are being pumped into shoring-up border surveillance while legally-required national human-rights monitors struggle with funding. Some EU states still don't have any monitors - despite a June deadline.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU ‘open’ to curbs on imports of Chinese chemicals and machinery, after hybrid-car deal
item.description: The European Commission “showed openness” to proposing trade "safeguards", a brake on imports that can cover entire sectors, such as chemicals and machinery.

item.title: [EU Observer] How Slovakia’s Fico became Putin’s top ally inside the EU
item.description: Slovak prime minister Robert Fico appears to have become Russia’s most prominent ally in the European Union, following the demise of Hungary's pro-Kremlin leader.

item.title: [DW] Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
item.description: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

item.title: [EU Observer] Zelensky urges unity, more money for Ukraine and sanctions on Russia ahead of key summit with EU leaders
item.description: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Brussels with two main requests for his meeting with EU leaders on Friday: more funds for Kyiv for defence and more sanctions against Russia.

item.title: [EU Observer] Train contract blow for Hungary’s richest man, plus Orbán will not mark 1956 anniversary (Day 156 of the Tisza government)
item.description: From derailing a flagship rail deal for Orbán-linked tycoon Lőrinc Mészáros to securing fresh EU and NGO money, the new Tisza government is rapidly unpicking the old system’s deals while racing to show voters concrete gains.

item.title: [EU Observer] Zelensky has had enough. Ukrainians strike refineries again — without Starlink (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,694)
item.description: Zelensky fumes over Trump-era limits on striking Russian oil while Ukrainian forces are pressing ahead with refinery and airbase hits.

item.title: [DW] EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
item.description: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

item.title: [DW] Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
item.description: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

item.title: [Financial Times] Apple blames ‘extraordinary’ demand as foldable iPhones sell out
item.description: Deliveries of the $2,000 Duo slip to 2027 within hours of going on sale

item.title: [Financial Times] Brent hits 5-month high above $110 on continued tension in Middle East
item.description: Oil prices jump on reports that Saudi Arabia-led forces intercepted and destroyed missiles aimed at important energy hubs

item.title: [Financial Times] Big Tech stocks suffer biggest weekly drop since ‘liberation day’
item.description: AI trade jitters send investors scrambling for government debt in a move that halts a months-long Treasury sell-off

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump’s press secretary Katie Zacharia fired after five days
item.description: Exit comes amid deepening turmoil for White House as midterm elections loom

item.title: [Financial Times] Israeli settlers attack Palestinians carrying out olive harvest in West Bank
item.description: Washington Post journalist among those injured during violence in the Palestinian territory

item.title: [DW] Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
item.description: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU leaders clash over migration, Ukraine and budget in Brussels — but delay big decisions
item.description: Leaders left crucial decisions on the bloc's long-term budget and Ukraine's financial needs to further gatherings in November and December.

item.title: [EU Observer] Denmark lashes out again at Sánchez over Spain’s migration regularisation, but EU summit avoids linking migration to crime
item.description: Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen lashed out again at Spanish leader Pedro Sánchez on migration during a summit debate in Brussels on Friday.

item.title: [DW] Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
item.description: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules?

item.title: [Financial Times] Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI wunderkind
item.description: The 29-year-old in charge of the company’s Superintelligence Labs is being touted as a potential successor to Mark Zuckerberg

item.title: [Politico Europe] 21 things we learned at the EU leaders’ summit
item.description: From the budget and migration to a terrible smell in the press room, here’s POLITICO’s rundown of the latest European Council.

item.title: [Politico Europe] In Europe’s tech capital, Irish labor unions are booming amid AI-driven layoffs
item.description: With Ireland's lucrative tech sector hit by waves of layoffs linked to AI, the country's nascent tech union has seen a spike in sign-ups from workers worried about their future.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Scottish government set to drop opposition to new oil and gas fields
item.description: The SNP has had a long-standing “presumption against” new oil fields.

item.title: [EU Observer] US-Russia ‘diesel deal’ could open door to wider sanctions relief, Zelensky warns as EU vows to keep supporting Ukraine
item.description: Volodomyr Zelensky flew into Brussels warning that Washington’s surprise ‘diesel deal’ with Moscow risks becoming the thin end of a wider sanctions rollback - just as Ukraine faces a brutal winter, dwindling air defences and a fresh scramble in EU capitals over money, missiles and frozen Russian billions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Germany and France want own ‘Made in Europe’ rules for cars, outside EU industrial policy
item.description: France and Germany want the rules for cars carved out of the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act and moved into a separate automotive package. Their joint paper also spells out how emissions targets will be weakened.

item.title: [Financial Times] Citi becomes latest US bank to restrict AI agents from accessing accounts
item.description: US lenders fear chatbots could shift billions of dollars in deposits to higher-yielding accounts

item.title: [EU Observer] Russian air force suffers worst day since Operation Spiderweb, as Ukraine destroys Su-34 strike aircraft on the ground (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,695)
item.description: While Washington quietly orders Starlink’s military network throttled and Moscow steps up long-range attacks, Ukrainian forces are still capable of audacious success.

item.title: [DW] Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
item.description: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

item.title: [DW] The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
item.description: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Zelenskyy warns 20M Ukrainians could flee to Europe if Russia wins war
item.description: The stark warning comes as Kyiv heads into a brutal winter and faces a cash crunch.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Denmark, Italy, Poland urge EU leaders to harden stance on irregular migration
item.description: Draft conclusions backed by Rome, Warsaw and Copenhagen say irregular migration is "negatively linked to crime rates."

item.title: [Politico Europe] Spanish opposition leader Feijóo calls for navy to be deployed to Ceuta
item.description: The conservatives have said they will implement measures to curb immigration if they win the upcoming snap elections.

item.title: [EU Observer] 16 EU states confirmed on board for plan to let countries close borders and freeze asylum
item.description: Over a dozen EU member states, along with the EU Commission, discussed migration at a pre-summit breakfast on Friday.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU prosecutors asked to investigate advisory body
item.description: Allegations of a conflict of interest at European Economic and Social Committee have been sent to EPPO.

item.title: [Politico Europe] France, Germany strike bargain on Made in Europe, car emissions
item.description: The compromise was reached after the German Social Democrats, the junior coalition partner in Friedrich Merz’s government, dropped their opposition.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Man arrested as police probe Your Party database dispute
item.description: There has been a long-running dispute surrounding the foundation of the new left-wing political party.

item.title: [DW] Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
item.description: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

item.title: [Financial Times] Republicans turn on Trump’s tariffs in battle for ‘political survival’
item.description: US president’s trade war has become an albatross for his party in crucial midterm election races

item.title: [EU Observer] Can the EU survive with far-right leaders running major member states? The answer is worrying
item.description: As the EU enters an unprecedented electoral supercycle, the question is whether it can defend its integrity as the forces challenging it gain influence over its institutions.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Too many lawyers’: the problem with Europe’s human rights NGOs
item.description: Traditionally, human rights NGOs have been staffed mainly by lawyers. This is understandable. But advocacy is becoming less effective because decision makers increasingly see supporting human rights as politically risky.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Are the Gilets Jaunes in France making a comeback?
item.description: Do you remember the Yellow Vests movement that shook France 2018? On TikTok, a young user has called for a national mobilisation on 17 October against the cost of living, and the video quickly went viral. So could the Yellow Vests make their big return?

item.title: [Financial Times] G7 economies plan simulated AI attacks on banks as cyber fears rise
item.description: Finance ministers agree to hold tabletop drills to prepare against future cyber attacks

item.title: [Financial Times] US business leaders are waking up to the perils of plutopopulism
item.description: Companies wanted a president who would cut taxes and rules, they got one who has blown holes in free trade and global alliances

item.title: [Financial Times] The secret fight around financial flows
item.description: Quicker responses to trade challenges mean companies can free up capital
